rules.what_is_seen: The longitudinal section draws the building as one very long, low two-storey bar roughly six times longer than the main block is tall, read as stacked horizontal bands of floor slabs, continuous sill and head lines and thin roof slabs, with only the chimney as a vertical element.

A longitudinal section cannot show the two parallel bars in plan, but the main two-storey bar steps down at its right end only to a lower single-storey element with a horizontally hatched parapet, so the long section reads asymmetrical, longer and lower toward one end.

The cut passes through a thick horizontally hatched masonry core at mid-length of the bar on the long axis, with the chimney rising from it above the roofs, the belvedere set over it, the floor slabs on both sides stopping against it and window bands continuing on both sides; no stair treads or hearth opening are identifiable at this scale.

A longitudinal section cannot show the plan shape of the end bays; the ends show only the window bands seen beyond and small sectioned end piers under the eaves, with no prow, angled glazing or main-level terrace identifiable.

The main roof and the belvedere roof are both drawn as very low-pitched thin slabs with thin fascias cantilevering about a window bay beyond the walls at each end, surfaces left plain, over flat ceilings at every storey; the single-storey element at the right end has a flat slab with a parapet rather than a roof.

A smaller third-storey block under its own low hipped roof sits set back on the main block beside the chimney near mid-length, and the masses step down to a single-storey element at the right end only, so the whole section is asymmetrical.

The main storey and belvedere show continuous bands of tall narrow lights between narrow piers set directly under the eaves with a continuous head at the ceiling line and a continuous sill, while the ground storey shows a separate band of short near-square lights between piers over a solid lower wall.

All cut masonry (garden walls, the central core, parapets and sectioned piers) is hatched with closely spaced continuous horizontal lines and no vertical joints, and the garden walls, parapets, pier heads and chimney top are finished with plain unhatched caps or coping bands.
Every light on the sheet is drawn as a plain frame with simple mullions and no glazing pattern at all, so the leaded-lattice claim cannot be tested here.

A detached low garden wall with a sectioned end pier and plain coping stands at the far left, a second low coursed wall with coping abuts the left end of the ground storey, and horizontally hatched parapet or planter blocks with stepped plain caps sit on the roof beside the chimney and on the right-end terrace; no urns or bowls are drawn.

The long wall seen beyond the cut is a continuous band of tall lights whose sills sit above floor level, but no balcony, door leaves or orientation are drawn, so the south glazed-door wall cannot be identified in this section.
No exterior door, steps, path, porch or canopy is drawn at either storey or at either end of the section; the main floor sits a storey above ground and shows only continuous window bands.
A single chimney rises above both roofs as a tall plain rectangular slab with a plain slightly projecting cap; no slot openings are drawn on the shaft in this section.

At building scale the only profiles drawn, the chimney cap, the pier caps and bases, the parapet steps and the wall copings, are plain stepped rectangular blocks with no curved profile; no interior trim or furniture is drawn.
The belvedere band is drawn as plain framed lights only with no stippled infill panels, which the sometimes-rule allows, so the panel claim cannot be tested here.

do_not_list.what_is_seen: No exterior door, steps, path, porch roof or canopy appears anywhere on the section, and the main floor shows only window bands.

The section is asymmetrical and stepped, with the belvedere off-centre beside the chimney, the lower single-storey element at the right end only and garden walls at the left end only; only the chimney slab is symmetrical about itself.
Nothing on the sheet carries carving, turning or applied ornament; the chimney, caps, copings and core are plain rectangular outlines and no mantel or surround is drawn.
Every hatched masonry element (garden walls, core blocks, parapets, sectioned piers) is rendered as continuous horizontal lines with no vertical joints.
Both roofs drawn, the main roof and the belvedere roof, are very low-pitched hipped slabs with deep overhangs and thin fascias; no gable or steep slope appears.
The chimney and its hatched masonry core are cut at mid-length of the bar between window bands on both sides, with no hearth or chimney at either outer end wall.

notes: Longitudinal section through the main bar (HABS sheet 8 of 10, labelled SECTION). Surfaces beyond the cut are left plain and all lights are frames and mullions only. Cut masonry is horizontally hatched: two low garden walls at the left, the central core beneath the chimney, a planter or parapet block on the roof right of the chimney, and the parapet of a single-storey element at the right end whose flat slab sits at main-floor level and reads as a terrace over a ground-level room. R10 and R13 are marked supported on the wall and chimney forms although urns and chimney slots are not drawn; R03 is supported on the core position although no stair or hearth opening is identifiable.
